newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 2.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 2.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Monday and main factors likely to affect trading:
* The will be prone to a correction due to the continuous rises last week, though the general mood will still be positive, Manuel Goseco, Dharmala Securities analyst said.

* Anscor-Hagedorn Securities vice-president Noel Reyes remains upbeat on the market and advises investors to load up a broad-based portfolio of stocks including real estate issues due to a projected lowering of interest rates for the rest of the year.
* On Friday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index closed 50.84 points higher at 2,809.45.
* The Dow Jones on Friday ended 0.86 points higher to 7,331.04. PLDT's ADR rose $0 1/2 to $57 7/8.

* Australian based soft drink bottler Coca Cola Amatil Ltd will concede San Miguel Corp a fourth board seat, The Australian Financial Review newspaper reported. C-C Amatil announced in April that it would acquire San Miguel's soft drink subsidiary in exchange for San Miguel taking a 25 percent stake in C-C Amatil. San Miguel would also gain three seats on the C-C Amatil 15-member expanded board.

* National Power Corp president Guido Delgado said it is planning to sell surplus electricity in the spot market on a daily basis and hopes to expand their plans later to include trading surplus electricity in the futures market.

* The Philippines, beaten by Thailand in a bidding war for General Motors Corp's manufacturing plant in Asia, is holding talks with the U.S. company on building a car component factory in the country, Trade Secretary Cesar Bautista said.
* Filinvest Development Corp said it sold about 3,500 square metres of land to San Miguel Corp and PLDT in the first quarter of the year.
* The Philippine Phospate Fertiliser Corp is planning to pre-sell about $500 million worth of its output to retire part of its $1.4 billion debt, Trade Secretary Cesar Bautista said.
* A Soriano Corp has reported a first quarter net income of 37.3 million pesos, sharply lower than the 97.52 million pesos level the first three months of 1996.

* The Philippine value of production index fell 2.3 percent in March to 460.2 from 470.8 in the same period last year, the National Statistics Office said. The volume of production also fell, dropping 3.6 percent to 154.6 in March.
* The Philippine peso closed higher at 26.375 to the dollar vs 26.374.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was steady at 16.03125 percent.

* Newspaper Manila Bulletin said the Department of Transportation and Communications expects to raise at least 30 billion pesos from the privatisation of its public calling offices, local exchanges and telegraph stations being planned next year.

* Philippine Times Journal said Filipino-Chinese tycoon Lucio Tan who controls 55 percent of Philipppine Airlines, is planning to undertake an initial public offering of the country's flag carries after the airline is pulled out of the red.

* Philippine Daily Inquirer said government will stick to its 7-8 percent economic growth target this year despite a lower-than-expected gross national product (GNP) during the first quarter of the year.

* The Philippine Star reported quoting the Central Bank managing director that the country's 6.1 percent GNP growth for the first quarter of 1997 reflects only economic output and that it has not been felt by a majority of the people, especially the poor.

* BusinessWorld said that the Senate ways and means committee has rejected the proposal of both local and foreign business groups to be allowed a choice on whether their corporate income tax will be based on net income or modified gross income.
The Senate and the House of Representatives have yet to pass a comprehensive tax bill essential for the country's exit from the International Monetary Fund programme this month.
